label: UniFi Gateway Fiber
description: A fibre-first gateway: four 2.5GbE RJ45, one 10GbE RJ45 and two 10G SFP+ cages, with 5 Gbps of IDS/IPS throughput. Built for a fibre WAN and a 10G core.
notes:
Vendor figures read 2026-11-19 from techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/uxg-fiber (HTTP 200, 649,433 B): Port Layout = 2.5 GbE RJ45 x4 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M), 10 GbE RJ45 x1 (10G/2.5G/1G), 10G SFP+ x2 (10G/1G); Max. WAN Port Count 6, Default WAN Ports (1) 10G SFP+ / (1) 10 GbE RJ45, IDS/IPS Throughput 5 Gbps, Form Factor compact desktop (212.8 x 127.6 x 30 mm), Max. Power Consumption 25 W excluding PoE output, Power Method = DC jack (54V DC/1.1A), Power Supply 54V DC/1.1A adapter included, Supported Voltage Range 100-240V AC, Heat Dissipation 85 BTU/hr excluding PoE output, Processor quad-core ARM Cortex-A73 at 2.2 GHz.
Power in: DC jack, no PoE input. All seven interfaces say poeIn: false so isPoePd()'s "unifi" match cannot draw 12.95 W on each of the five copper sockets (64.75 W) on a box fed by a 54 V DC jack.
PoE out: the gateway does source power, and it is now written. The tech-spec table prints "PoE Budget = 30W", "Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE = PoE+ 30W" and "Voltage Range PoE Mode = 50-57V", and store.ui.com/us/en/products/uxg-fiber (HTTP 200, 476,892 B, displaySku "UXG-Fiber (30W)") says "Integrated 4-port switch with (1) PoE+ port". Neither host numbers the port, so eth0 carries it - the same convention as devices/ubiquiti/ucg-fiber.json, the Cloud Gateway Fiber twin of this box, which records the identical 30 W / one-PoE+ census; the count and class are the vendor's, only the numbering is ours. Before this the row declared no poe-pse and no budget, so `show power inline` refused and the allocator could not power one AP from a box the vendor says can power one. Still not modelled, and not because of a missing source: no datasheet exists for this SKU (the store payload carries datasheet: null and dl.ui.com/ds/uxg-fiber_ds.pdf lands on the 609,911-byte techspecs front page), so the per-port ceiling comes from the rendered table rather than a PDF.

Layer 2: Ubiquiti's controller device database classifies this SKU as a switch - https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, read 2026-11-21) lists UXG-Fiber deviceCapabilities GATEWAY, SWITCH, APPLICATION_GATEWAY, HAS_CLIENTS and draws its panel as `01 02 03 04 05 06 07` - and the vendor tech-spec table publishes the bridge's forwarding database at https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/uxg-fiber (HTTP 200, 649,433 B, read 2026-11-21), which prints "MAC Address Table Size = 4,000"; no LACP and no segmentation row appears, so neither is claimed. A MAC address table is a bridge FDB; a gateway that only routed would hold neither it nor a LAG. While the row shipped without `l2-forward` its copper sockets were routed interfaces: `switchport access vlan 10` was answered with "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability", and two hosts on eth0 and eth1 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP ("not addressed to this device"). WAN side unchanged: "Default WAN Ports = (1) 10G SFP+ / (1) 10 GbE RJ45", "Max. WAN Port Count = 6"; eth4 is the only 10 GbE RJ45 but the row keeps every socket interchangeable rather than inventing a saved lab's WAN choice.

poe.note: 30 W, the vendor's whole published budget: the tech-spec table prints "PoE Budget = 30W", "Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE = PoE+ 30W" and "Voltage Range PoE Mode = 50-57V" (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/uxg-fiber, HTTP 200, 649,433 B, read 2026-11-19), and the store page for the same SKU states the count and class in prose: "Integrated 4-port switch with (1) PoE+ port", displaySku "UXG-Fiber (30W)" (https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/uxg-fiber, HTTP 200, 476,892 B, read 2026-11-19). Neither host numbers the port, so eth0 carries it - the same placement convention as devices/ubiquiti/ucg-fiber.json, the Cloud Gateway Fiber twin of this box, which records the identical 30 W / one-PoE+ census. The numbering is a convention; the count (1), the class (802.3at) and the ceiling (30 W) are the vendor's. One 802.3at port at its ceiling exactly consumes the budget, so it never binds above a single full-power AP.
